name: The Collected Poems of Jaden Abora
subtitle: Non-magical book, found in Horus's basement crates
body:
A slim, well-worn volume bound in gray cloth. No author note on the spine. The title page reads: The Collected Poems of Jaden Abora — For Those Who Wander Between.

Five poems, handwritten in a clear script. The margins of two pages have small annotations in a different hand — Horus's, presumably.

I. THE HIVE AT THIRD BELL

The smoke here remembers
every fire it came from.
The stones have absorbed
so many arguments
they hum at certain frequencies.

I have learned to walk
through the parts of the city
that are mostly memory —
the places where something happened
and never finished happening.

II. PORTALS

Every door here
has a key that isn't a key.
A thought, a word, a way
of holding your hands.

I used to think
that was a metaphor
for how understanding works.

Now I think it is
exactly what it says.
The door opens
when you mean it.

III. THE DEAD

The Dustmen say
this is the waiting room.
I believe them
more than I used to.

The things I carry
feel lighter here.
I don't know if that's
the planes doing something to me
or me finally putting things down.

IV. DEBT

A man I trusted
kept meticulous records.
Every favor. Every coin.
He showed me the ledger once.
I was not in it
the way I thought I was.

I have been more careful
with my accounting
ever since.

V. ON LEAVING

Every portal goes somewhere.
That is the thing to hold onto
when the key is strange
and the door doesn't look like a door.

Somewhere is enough.
I have been to worse places
than somewhere.

name: Otik's Frying Pan
subtitle: Magical weapon, shield, and meal-prep tool
body:
A cast-iron frying pan, well-seasoned, with a handle wrapped in worn leather. It looks like it has been used to cook many meals. It has also been used to hit many people. Both uses show.

The pan radiates faint conjuration magic. The enchantment was placed by a halfling cleric named Otik who could not afford a proper weapon. He made do.
mechanics:
Weapon: Simple melee weapon, 1d6 bludgeoning (versatile 1d8). Counts as a +1 magical weapon. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or be dazed until the start of their next turn (can move or take an action, not both).

Shield: Can be worn on the arm as a shield (+2 AC) while still being usable as a weapon. Using it as a shield does not require proficiency.

Meal Prep: Once per short rest, the wielder can use the pan to conjure a simple hot meal: enough food for up to six people. The meal provides the nourishment of a full ration. It appears in the pan already cooked. It does not taste like anything in particular but it is filling.

name: The Pet Rock
subtitle: Wondrous item (rare), weekly diamond chance
body:
A smooth gray river stone, palm-sized, with no distinguishing marks. It is warm. It has been warm since the party found it. It is always exactly body temperature, regardless of environment.

Horus's notes (marginal, on the inventory list in the basement) say only: "Don't lose the rock."
mechanics: Once per week: At dawn on Sunday (or equivalent), roll a d100. On a result of 98–00, the rock transforms into a flawless diamond worth 500 gp and a new, identical rock appears in the same location. The rock does not otherwise do anything. It does not speak. It does not move. It is warm.

name: Elemental Bolt Pouch
subtitle: 6 elemental bolts, type determined on draw
body: A small leather pouch containing six crossbow bolts. Each bolt is tipped with a crystallized elemental fragment: some fire, some ice, some lightning, some force. They are not labeled. The pouch's enchantment randomizes which type you draw.
mechanics:
On draw: Roll a d6 to determine the bolt's element:

RollElementEffect
1Fire+1d6 fire, target must save DC 13 or catch fire
2Cold+1d6 cold, target speed reduced by 10 ft until end of their next turn
3Lightning+1d6 lightning, arcs to nearest creature within 10 ft for 1d4
4Acid+1d6 acid, -1 to target's AC until cleaned (action)
5Thunder+1d6 thunder, target pushed 10 ft
6Force+1d8 force, no save or secondary effect

The pouch has 6 bolts. They do not replenish.

name: Ioun Stone (Stone 1)
subtitle: Held by Grey Reed at campaign open
body:
An ioun stone of unusual clarity — pale, nearly translucent, orbiting with a faint resonant hum. Grey Reed has possessed it for at least six years. He uses it for contact juggling. Whether this is habit, demonstration, or a method of studying it is unclear.

Its specific function has not been revealed to the party. Grey Reed knows what it does.

callout.label: GM ONLY
callout.text: Stone 1 is in Grey Reed's possession at campaign open. Do not confirm its location or function to the party until the endgame. The contact juggling is intentional misdirection — it makes the stone visible before the party understands what they're looking at.

name: Ioun Stone (Stone 2)
subtitle: Inside the bag of withholding; Wizard Shop at Cinderbark Crossing
body:
The second stone is sealed inside the bag of withholding — a bag that will not open for anyone who did not create it. The bag is in Horus House's basement. The party has possession of the bag from Session One. They will not be able to open it until Arc 2.

The bag was originally commissioned by Horus from a Wizard Shop at Cinderbark Crossing. The shop has since closed. The wizard who made it is not findable through normal means. Arc 2's research component involves tracing the bag's provenance and finding a way to open it without destroying the contents.

callout.label: LOCATION
callout.text: Bag of withholding is in Horus House basement, in a wooden crate under a canvas cover. The party has it from Session One. They cannot open it yet.
